sources.entry: Termstead - Native SSH client with a session tree, jump hosts and SFTP beside the terminal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/pkhorenyan/termstead) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Termstead
summary.one_liner: Termstead is a free, open-source native SSH and RDP client for macOS that offers a MobaXterm-style server tree, tabs, jump hosts, tunnels and SFTP.
use_cases: Manage many servers in a tree of saved sessions
Connect to servers through bastion or jump hosts
Set up local, remote and SOCKS tunnels to databases or dashboards
Open remote desktop (RDP) sessions alongside terminals
Transfer and edit files on remote servers from Finder
Run one command across several servers with broadcast input
summary.what_it_does: Termstead is a macOS app that organizes SSH and RDP connections into a tree of groups, colors and favorites, with terminals and remote desktops opened as tabs that can be split into panes. It supports jump hosts (ProxyJump-style chains), local, remote and SOCKS tunnels with start/stop switches, and SFTP-style file transfer and in-place editing over an open connection. Each tab runs the system ssh, so the user's agent, ~/.ssh/config and known_hosts are used, and saved passwords are supplied only for the matching user@host. The page also describes a status bar showing server CPU, memory, disk and network, and eight color themes.
notable: Runs the system OpenSSH rather than its own SSH code, so ~/.ssh/config and ProxyJump work as in Terminal
Built-in RDP sessions via a sandboxed FreeRDP engine, in the same tree as terminals
Saved passwords are offered only for the exact user@host they were saved for; sessions stored as a local JSON file with no accounts or analytics
Installable via Homebrew cask; signed, notarized, and requires macOS 14 or later
caveats: macOS only (macOS 14 Sonoma or later; Apple silicon and Intel)
Listed as a MobaXterm alternative; it is not a Windows client, and the page describes only Mac support
